ranking.rationale: Exact fit: the Wish asks for a pocket-size, support-free tactile puzzle with exactly three robust parts, one memorable transformation, inspectable clearances, and no hardware or brittle snap.
Strong fit for a compact twist transformation and two intentional end states, but its normal deployable-linkage craft would add complexity beyond this three-part puzzle.
Strong fit for three support-free parts and one repeatable motion, though its usual press/spin toy emphasis is less puzzle- and reveal-centered than Mira Fold.
Could build a wish-specific kinetic reveal, but a machine-first spectacle would overcomplicate the quiet pocket object requested here.
Understands hand-powered reveals, yet the Wish does not depend on light, shadow, aperture, silhouette projection, or moire.
Its captive-motion discipline is adjacent, but loops, crossings, and topology are not the requested visual or mechanical language.
Flat-print robustness and negative-space patterning are useful, but the request is a single transformation puzzle rather than a modular arrangement system.
A miniature world is adjacent to the revealed storm scene, but no personal subject, real place, relationship, or recognition reference is present.
The object could illustrate weather symbols, but the Wish asks for tactile surprise rather than a testable science or mathematics phenomenon.
The word puzzle does not imply a rules-driven tabletop game, players, turns, or simulation-dependent balance.
No abstract strategy board, piece system, combinatorial depth, or competitive play is requested.
There is no known tabletop classic to preserve or personalize.
